We really need to strengthen the middle order so that the final scorers are in the fifties, not eighties and nineties, plus we need the the occasional guest appearances by some of our stars: Darren Mead, Matt Yates, Chris Sweeney and a fit again Kassa.

At a time when 14k of cross country seems unpopular among our members, 1500m star Matt Yates fancied having a run and, donning a brand new pair of spikes and a Belgrave vest to tackle the Showground and farmland of Newark, proceeded to give us our best individual position since .. well, you tell us.

Next up was Matt Yates and he set about the teams ahead as if it was war. He had some large gaps to bridge but nevertheless, Birchfield, Morpeth, Liverpool and Sheffield were just some of the teams that fell to his all-devouring stride and he must have been delighted at out-running Sale's Kevin McKay by ten seconds.

While Blackheath went ahead for the first time our own Jim Estall did plenty of damage himself as he clocked our third fastest long leg and recovered five places. Now it was up to Matt Yates to impose himself on the field.
